questions.problem: The vector $a$ is directed due north-east and $|\,a\,|=7$, while the vector $b$ is directed due north-west and $|\,b\,|=7.$ Which of the following is a unit vector that is parallel to $a+b?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we have to find $a+b.$ According to the triangle law of addition, the resultant $a+b$ goes from the tail of $a$ to the head of $b:$   

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251721/assets/9468530a650f0bee117a4254aa87b5954c7bbbe2684d95f9db3f9961026abcb2.png)

To find the unit vector corresponding to $a+b,$ we have to divide by the magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{a+b}{|a+b|}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the magnitude, first notice that we obtain a right triangle. So, we can use the Pythagorean theorem:

$$
\begin{aligned}{|a+b|}^{2} & ={|a|}^{2}+{|b|}^{2} \\  & ={7}^{2}+{7}^{2} \\  & =98\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the magnitude is

$$
|a+b|=\sqrt{98}=7\sqrt{2},
$$

and the corresponding unit vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{a+b}{|a+b|} \\  & =\frac{1}{7\sqrt{2}}(a+b).\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
A **unit vector** is a vector whose magnitude is equal to $1.$ 

Given any vector $\mathbf a$, we can create a unit vector $\mathbf u$ by dividing $\mathbf a$ by its magnitude $|\, \mathbf{a} \,|,$ as follows:

$$
\mathbf{u} = \dfrac{ \mathbf{a} }{ |\,\mathbf{a}\,| }
$$

For example, if $|\,\mathbf{a}\,|=2,$ then the unit vector is

$$
\mathbf{u} = \dfrac{\mathbf{a}}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \mathbf{a}.
$$
